sources.title: Law of the RSFSR No. 1098-I of 24 April 1991 'On the President of the RSFSR' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Rossiyskaya Gazeta of 27 April 1991; Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1991 No. 17, art. 512

claims.text: Citing the will of the people expressed at the first RSFSR referendum of 17 March 1991, the RSFSR Supreme Soviet adopts a law under which the President of the RSFSR is the highest official of the RSFSR and the head of executive power in the RSFSR. The President may not be a people's deputy, suspends membership of political parties and public associations while in office and holds no other post.
claims.uncertainty: Adoption day only. Resolution 1099-I of the same day put the law into force from the moment of publication, and that day is not verified. The referendum result was not reviewed from a primary record. The text does not use the term 'head of state'.

claims.text: A citizen aged 35 to 65 may be elected President for five years, and no one may be President for more than two consecutive terms. The President is elected by universal, equal and direct suffrage by secret ballot; any other election, appointment or assumption of the powers is unlawful and void. A Vice-President, whose candidacy the presidential candidate proposes, is elected at the same time.
claims.uncertainty: Statutory rules; not evidence of any election, term start or term end. Article 3 leaves the procedure for election and for assuming office to separate laws.

claims.text: Article 4 prescribes the oath the President takes on assuming office. Article 7 has the Vice-President substitute for the President in his absence, and Article 11 gives the Vice-President the President's powers on the President's removal, resignation, inability to exercise the powers or death.
claims.uncertainty: Rules only; no acting arrangement is attested by this text.

claims.text: The law is signed by B. N. Yeltsin as Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet, Moscow, House of Soviets of the RSFSR, 24 April 1991, No. 1098-I.
claims.uncertainty: One signed office observation, recorded as a claim only: this packet has no RSFSR Supreme Soviet institution, and a signature is not a chairmanship term.

sources.scope_note: Original edition (rdk=0) of the law creating the office. The portal card cites Rossiyskaya Gazeta of 27 April 1991 and Vedomosti 1991 No. 17, art. 512; neither issue was inspected, so 27 April is not recorded as the entry-into-force day, and 24 April is the adoption day only. The portal also carries an edition 1 annotated with Presidential Decree No. 2288 of 24 December 1993; that later status is outside this packet and is not imported.

sources.title: Rosarkhiv virtual exhibition item 09-36: Law of the RSFSR 'On the President of the RSFSR', 24 April 1991 (GARF original)

The exhibition previews of leaf 75 (heading, a preamble citing the referendum of 17 March 1991, Articles 1-3) and leaf 79 (Articles 9-11, Yeltsin's signature and 'Москва, Дом Советов РСФСР, 24 апреля 1991 года, № 1098-I') agree with the portal text.
claims.locator: Exhibit caption; preview images of L. 75 and L. 79
claims.uncertainty: The previews are low-resolution exhibition thumbnails; the full-size images return HTTP 404 from every capture tried. Leaves 76-78 were not viewed.

sources.scope_note: The 2012 exhibition page (caption and transcribed extracts of Articles 1, 5 and 10) and two preview images, read from Internet Archive captures because the official host refused connections. The transcribed extracts agree with the portal text of Law 1098-I.

sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1991 No. 17, art. 513

claims.text: The Supreme Soviet puts the Law of the RSFSR 'On the President of the RSFSR' into force from the moment of its publication and submits the law to the Congress of People's Deputies for approval; signed B. N. Yeltsin, Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet, Moscow, House of Soviets of the RSFSR, 24 April 1991, No. 1099-I.
claims.locator: Operative text; signature and date block
claims.uncertainty: 24 April is the date of this resolution, not the day the law entered into force. The publication that brought the law into force is not identified: the portal card for 1098-I cites Rossiyskaya Gazeta of 27 April 1991, which was not inspected, so no entry-into-force date is recorded.

sources.scope_note: Resolution setting entry into force from publication. Its own gazette citation is Vedomosti 1991 No. 17, art. 513 (the law itself is art. 512). The operative text prints the law's title with a typographical slip ('О Президента РСФСР').

sources.title: Resolution of the RSFSR Congress of People's Deputies No. 1325-I of 22 May 1991 'On candidates for President of the RSFSR' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1991 No. 21, art. 709

claims.text: After a report by V. I. Kazakov, chairman of the Central Electoral Commission for the election of the President of the RSFSR, the Congress notes that six candidates are registered under Article 8 of the election law: Bakatin, Yeltsin, Zhirinovsky, Makashov, Ryzhkov and Tuleev. Because Zhirinovsky, nominated by the Liberal Democratic Party, needs the support of at least one fifth of all people's deputies to be put on the ballot, it orders a secret vote on supporting him.
claims.uncertainty: The candidates' individual registration dates and the result of the support vote are not in this text. That six candidates were on the ballot is attested separately by the CEC communication (ru_cec_election_voting_19910612).

sources.scope_note: Congress resolution on the registered candidates. Gazette citation: Vedomosti 1991 No. 21, art. 709.

sources.title: Law of the RSFSR No. 1326-I of 24 May 1991 'On amendments and additions to the Constitution (Basic Law) of the RSFSR' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1991 No. 22, art. 776

claims.text: The Congress of People's Deputies amends the RSFSR Constitution, inserting Chapter 13-1 'President of the RSFSR' (Articles 121-1 to 121-11): the President is the highest official and head of executive power, elected for five years; the chapter sets the oath and a Vice-President elected jointly who exercises the President's powers on the President's removal, resignation, inability or death. The new Article 122 makes the Council of Ministers accountable to the President. Signed B. N. Yeltsin, Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet, Moscow, Kremlin, 24 May 1991, No. 1326-I.
claims.locator: Point 11 (Chapter 13-1), point 12 (Article 122); signature and date block
claims.uncertainty: Constitutional text as adopted on 24 May 1991, a separate event from the 24 April statute. Its own entry into force and later amendment history were not reviewed.

sources.scope_note: Constitutional amendment writing the presidency into the RSFSR Constitution; only points 11 and 12 and the signature block are imported. Gazette citation: Vedomosti 1991 No. 22, art. 776.

sources.title: Rosarkhiv virtual exhibition item 09-37: Resolution of the Central Electoral Commission for the Election of the President of the RSFSR 'On the results of the election of the President of the RSFSR', 19 June 1991, with the CEC communication (GARF original)
sources.publisher: Federal Archival Agency (Rosarkhiv), 2012 virtual exhibition; original held by GARF, F. 10026, Op. 8, D. 204

claims.text: CEC resolution No. 20-25 of 19 June 1991 takes note of chairman V. I. Kazakov's report on the results of the election of the President of the RSFSR, approves the text of the CEC communication on the results and orders the communication published through TASS in the republican and local press; signed by V. Kazakov (chairman) and V. Prozorov (secretary).
claims.uncertainty: The TASS publication date is not given; that publication is the 'official announcement' from which Article 1 of Law 1494-I counts one month. The archival leaf is unconfirmed: the exhibit caption gives GARF F. 10026, Op. 8, D. 204, L. 6-7 and captions the three images L. 6, L. 6 ob. and L. 7, while the handwritten folio numbers on the images read 5, 6 and 7.

claims.text: The communication approved by that resolution reports that the CEC examined the district commissions' protocols on the results of voting on 12 June 1991 in the election of the President of the RSFSR, held in 88 electoral districts, and that six candidates were on the ballot.
claims.uncertainty: The voting day as the communication states it. It is not the determination or approval of the result (19 June), not a publication date and not a term start. The communication is undated; it is dated by the resolution that approved it.

claims.text: As approved on 19 June 1991: 106,484,518 citizens were on the voter lists and 79,498,240 (74.66 per cent) took part; votes for the candidates were Yeltsin 45,552,041 (57.30 per cent), Ryzhkov 13,395,335 (16.85), Zhirinovsky 6,211,007 (7.81), Tuleev 5,417,464 (6.81), Makashov 2,969,511 (3.74) and Bakatin 2,719,757 (3.42); 1,716,757 ballots (2.16 per cent) were declared invalid.
claims.uncertainty: Result figures as determined and approved on 19 June; the vote itself took place on 12 June (ru_cec_election_voting_19910612). Votes against each candidate, ballots with every name struck out and the results annulled at two polling stations are in the communication but not imported.

claims.text: Under Article 15 of the RSFSR law on the election of the President, the communication states that Boris Nikolaevich Yeltsin, born 1931, Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet, was elected President of the RSFSR, having received more than half the votes of those who took part, and that Alexander Vladimirovich Rutskoi, chairman of a Supreme Soviet committee, is considered elected Vice-President of the RSFSR.
claims.uncertainty: An election result, not an oath or an assumption of office. Yeltsin is still described as Supreme Soviet Chairman. No holder observation starts here.

sources.scope_note: The 2012 exhibition page (caption and transcription) and three facsimile images of the GARF originals, read from Internet Archive captures because the official host refused connections. All three images were viewed at full size and agree with the exhibition transcription.

source_review.note: Codex's 27 September 2026 sample requested the official page URL, not this recorded response, and timed out. Between 2026-09-27T23:40:28Z and 2026-09-28T00:55:36Z projects.rusarchives.ru again opened no TCP connection on port 443 or 80, nor rusarchives.ru on 443 (8 attempts in all), so no live identity exists. The recorded raw Internet Archive capture, requested with Accept-Encoding: identity and served uncompressed, returned 15,700 bytes with the recorded SHA-256 at 2026-09-27T23:42:08Z and at 2026-09-28T00:55:57Z; captures 20210225052658, 20210511100649, 20210612153223, 20210924090951, 20230929012544 return the same bytes, and the 2019 captures differ only in the analytics script. The three facsimiles reproduce their recorded identities. Content comparison: the caption (GARF F. 10026, Op. 8, D. 204, L. 6-7), the image captions (L. 6, L. 6 ob., L. 7) and facsimile 1 (No. 20-25 of 19 June 1991, points 1-3, signed by V. Kazakov and V. Prozorov) agree with every claim; the leaf discrepancy against the handwritten folios 5, 6 and 7 is unchanged and unresolved. No claim or date changed. Per-capture identities are in the extract's source_review.

sources.title: Law of the RSFSR No. 1494-I of 27 June 1991 'On the assumption of office of the President of the RSFSR' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1991 No. 26, art. 880

claims.text: A President elected under the RSFSR Constitution takes office no later than one month after the official announcement of the election results, swearing an oath to the people at a solemn session of the highest body of state power, after which the State Anthem is played. From the moment of the oath the President and the Vice-President are deemed to have taken office, to have given up their deputies' mandates and to be released from other posts. The Council of Ministers resigns before the new President within ten days. The law enters into force on adoption.
claims.uncertainty: Rule statute; it gives no oath date. The oath date comes from the stenographic record (ru_steno_oath_19910710).

claims.text: The law is signed by B. N. Yeltsin as Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet, Moscow, House of Soviets of the RSFSR, 27 June 1991, No. 1494-I.
claims.uncertainty: After the 12 June vote and the 19 June result he still signed as Chairman. Recorded as a claim only; it does not fix when that chairmanship ended (see ru_res_1595i_yeltsin_release_19910710).

sources.scope_note: Rule statute for the assumption of office. Gazette citation: Vedomosti 1991 No. 26, art. 880. The portal card marks the law as no longer in force; when and how it lapsed is outside this packet.

sources.title: Stenographic record: solemn session of the Congress of People's Deputies of the RSFSR dedicated to the assumption of office of the first President of the RSFSR, Boris Nikolaevich Yeltsin, 10 July 1991 (Moscow, 1991, 216 pp.)
sources.publisher: Congress of People's Deputies of the RSFSR (stenographic report, Moscow 1991); digital copy by the Boris Yeltsin Presidential Library, original copy held by the Russian Book Chamber

claims.text: The solemn session of the fifth (extraordinary) Congress of People's Deputies of the RSFSR, dedicated to the assumption of office of the first President of the RSFSR, met in the Kremlin Palace of Congresses on 10 July 1991 at 10 o'clock, chaired by R. I. Khasbulatov, First Deputy Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet.
claims.uncertainty: The printed opening hour is not the minute of the oath, which the record does not print.

claims.text: The chair invites the first President, Boris Nikolaevich Yeltsin, to take the oath. Under the speaker heading 'Yeltsin B. N., President of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic' he recites the presidential oath; the State Anthem follows, and screens show the RSFSR State Flag being raised over the President's residence in the Kremlin.
claims.uncertainty: The stenographer's heading is not an appointment instrument. The legal effect of the oath comes from Article 3 of Law 1494-I; the record gives no clock time for it.

claims.text: In his address Yeltsin refers to Alexander Vladimirovich Rutskoi as the first Vice-President of Russia.
claims.uncertainty: A speech reference. Rutskoi's assumption of office rests on Article 3 of Law 1494-I and resolution 1596-I.

claims.text: The chair gives the floor to 'the President of the USSR, Mikhail Sergeyevich Gorbachev', who says that the solemn act of the oath and assumption of office of the first President of the Russian Federation has just taken place and congratulates Yeltsin on his election as President of the republic.
claims.locator: Printed page 12 (image 14), last paragraphs; printed page 13 (image 15), opening paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: A congratulatory speech that corroborates the sequence only. It is not used as a holder observation on the USSR packet's su_president role and maps no USSR office to the RSFSR presidency.

sources.scope_note: Only 20 of the 216 pages are public. Printed pages 3-7 and 12-13 (images 5-9, 14 and 15) and the cover were read in full; later speeches and closing formalities were not reviewed. The chair's greeting on printed page 3 of 'the President of the country' M. S. Gorbachev and 'the Chairman of the USSR Supreme Soviet' A. I. Lukyanov is not imported. The item page is a dynamic Drupal page, so no page hash is asserted; the page images reproduce exactly.

sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1991 No. 28, art. 970

claims.text: Citing Yeltsin's assumption of office as President of the RSFSR under Article 121-1 of the RSFSR Constitution and Article 3 of the law on the assumption of office, the Congress releases Boris Nikolaevich Yeltsin from the duties of Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet and deems his powers as people's deputy for Sverdlovsk national-territorial district No. 74 terminated; signed R. claims.uncertainty: A same-day act that gives no hour and does not itself confer the presidency. The release from the chairmanship is recorded as a claim only, because this packet has no RSFSR Supreme Soviet institution.

sources.title: Law of the RSFSR No. 2094-I of 25 December 1991 'On changing the name of the state Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1992 No. 2, art. 62

claims.text: The RSFSR Supreme Soviet enacts that the state Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR) is henceforth to be called the Russian Federation (Russia), a name to be used in official acts, in state symbols and in the names of state bodies; the former names may be used in official paperwork (forms, seals and stamps) during 1992; a draft law amending the Constitution and the Declaration of State Sovereignty is to be put to the Congress of People's Deputies; the law enters into force on the day of its adoption, 25 December 1991.
claims.uncertainty: A renaming of the RSFSR, not a succession from the USSR and not an act of a USSR organ. Adoption and entry into force fall on the same day under point 5. The constitutional amendment it asks the Congress to adopt was not reviewed.

claims.text: The portal text prints the signature block 'Президент Российской Федерации Б.Ельцин, Москва, Дом Советов России, 25 декабря 1991 года, № 2094-I'.
claims.uncertainty: Published text only. The signed GARF original (ru_garf_law_2094i_original_19911225) reads 'Президент РСФСР' and 'Дом Советов РСФСР'. The published title is not evidence of the title under which the law was signed, and neither form is used as a holder observation.

sources.scope_note: The renaming law; it is why the RSFSR presidency is filed in this packet. Gazette citation: Vedomosti 1992 No. 2, art. 62. Its published signature title differs from the signed original (see ru_garf_exhibit_law_2094i).

sources.title: Rosarkhiv virtual exhibition item 10-04: Law of the RSFSR 'On changing the name of the state Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic', 25 December 1991 (GARF original)
sources.publisher: Federal Archival Agency (Rosarkhiv), 2012 virtual exhibition; original held by GARF, F. 10026, Op. 1, D. 577, L. 103

claims.text: Rosarkhiv describes the item as the typescript original with the autograph signature of the President of the RSFSR, B. N. Yeltsin (GARF F. 10026, Op. 1, D. 577, L. 103). The facsimile shows points 1-5 as in the portal text and the signature block 'Президент РСФСР ... Б.Ельцин, Москва, Дом Советов РСФСР, 25 декабря 1991 года, № 2094-I'.
claims.uncertainty: The signed form. The published text prints 'President of the Russian Federation' (ru_law_2094i_published_signature_19911225). A signature title is an office observation, not a term, and is not used as a holder observation.

sources.scope_note: The 2012 exhibition page (caption and transcription) and the facsimile of the signed original, read from Internet Archive captures because the official host refused connections. The facsimile was viewed at full size.

sources.title: Law of the Russian Federation No. 2708-I of 21 April 1992 'On amendments and additions to the Constitution (Basic Law) of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal list cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RF i Verkhovnogo Soveta RF 1992 No. 20, art. 1084

claims.text: The Congress of People's Deputies of the Russian Federation amends the RSFSR Constitution 'in connection with the change of the state's name' to 'Российская Федерация - Россия': Article 1 is restated (the names Russian Federation and Russia are equivalent); in the Constitution's title and preamble the old name and 'РСФСР' become 'Российской Федерации - России'; and in the headings of listed sections and chapters (including chapters '13-16') and in listed articles (including '102-123', the range holding Articles 121-1 to 121-11 on the President) the old name and 'РСФСР' are replaced by 'Российская Федерация' / 'Российской Федерации'. The office's constitutional title thereby reads 'Президент Российской Федерации'.
claims.uncertainty: The law replaces words in listed articles and never names the title 'Президент РСФСР' itself; the retitling follows from the article list. Whether 'глав ... 13-16' covers the heading of Chapter 13-1 is not stated. Adoption day, not entry into force (see ru_law_2708i_in_force_on_publication_19920421). A renaming of the title, not a new office or a new holder.

claims.text: Point 50 restates Article 121-8 in terms of 'Президент Российской Федерации': the President issues decrees and orders on matters within his competence, his decrees are binding throughout the Russian Federation and may not contradict the Constitution and laws, and he may suspend acts of republic executives.
claims.uncertainty: Operative constitutional text using the new title; procedure only, not a date for the office or a holder.

claims.text: Point 63: the Law is put into effect from the day of its publication.
claims.uncertainty: The publication day is not verified: the portal cites only Vedomosti 1992 No. 20, art. 1084, and no newspaper issue was inspected. No entry-into-force day is recorded.

claims.text: The published text ends 'Президент Российской Федерации Б.ЕЛЬЦИН, Москва, Кремль, 21 апреля 1992 года, N 2708-I'.
claims.uncertainty: Published text only; the signed original was not reviewed, and for Law 2094-I the published title (President of the Russian Federation) differs from the signed original (President of the RSFSR). A signature is an office observation, not a term; it is a claim only and is not used as a holder observation on ru_president or ru_rsfsr_president.

sources.scope_note: Constitutional amendment text: procedure only, never a date for the office or a holder. The preamble, Section I points 1-4 and 17, Section V point 50, Section VIII points 63-68 and the signature block were read; other amendments were skimmed. The newspaper publication that brought it into force was not inspected (portal citation: Vedomosti 1992 No. 20, art. 1084).

sources.title: Ruling (Postanovlenie) of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation No. 9-P of 30 November 1992 on the constitutionality of Presidential decrees of 23 and 25 August and 6 November 1991 and of the CPSU and CP RSFSR
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii'; the portal list cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RF i Verkhovnogo Soveta RF 1993 No. 11, art. 400

claims.text: In its own voice the Court styles the author of the 1991 acts under review as the 'Президент Российской Федерации': it hears representatives of the President of the Russian Federation 'как стороны, издавшей рассматриваемые Указы' (decrees No. 79 of 23 August 1991, No. 90 of 25 August 1991 and No. 169 of 6 November 1991, titled 'Указов Президента Российской Федерации'), and it says that 'Президент Российской Федерации издал 20 июля 1991 года Указ' and, in August 1991, 'издал ряд указов'. The form 'Президент РСФСР' appears only inside quoted titles of other bodies' acts (a CP RSFSR Central Committee resolution of 6 August 1991 and the Supreme Soviet resolution of 21 August 1991).
claims.locator: Heading; list of participants; reasoning (установил), part I
claims.uncertainty: Ties the renamed title to the office that issued the 1991 acts, not to a person: the ruling does not name Yeltsin, and the 1991 decrees themselves (signed as President of the RSFSR) were not reviewed. A retrospective styling in a judgment of 30 November 1992; a claim only, never a boundary or a basis for merging ru_rsfsr_president and ru_president holders.

sources.scope_note: Searched rather than read in full (372 KB): the heading, the list of participants, the reasoning passages that name the President, and every occurrence of 'Президент РСФСР' and 'Ельцин' (no line names Yeltsin). The findings on the CPSU are outside this packet.

sources.title: Conclusion (Zaklyuchenie) of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation of 23 March 1993 on the conformity with the Constitution of the actions and decisions of the President of the Russian Federation B. N. Yeltsin connected with his Address to the citizens of Russia of 20 March 1993
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii'; the portal list cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RF i Verkhovnogo Soveta RF 1993 No. 13, art. 466

claims.text: The Court's conclusion of 23 March 1993 is titled as concerning the actions and decisions of 'Президента Российской Федерации Б.Н.Ельцина' and records that on 20 March 1993 'Президент Российской Федерации Б.Н.Ельцин' addressed the citizens of Russia on television.
claims.uncertainty: A contemporaneous primary record that names Yeltsin under the renamed title; an office observation on the day of the conclusion, not a start, a term or a continuation. The Court's findings about the address are not imported. Before the 1993 Constitution the office was not defined as head of state (ru_const1993_art80_head_of_state), so it is a claim on ru_president only: no ru_president holder is recorded for 1991-1996.

sources.scope_note: Title, composition, the first findings paragraph and the heads of two separate opinions were read. The findings on the 20 March 1993 address are outside this packet and are not assessed.

sources.title: Determination (Opredelenie) of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation No. 134-O of 5 November 1998 on the interpretation of Article 81(3) and point 3 of Section Two 'Final and transitional provisions' of the Constitution
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii'; the portal list cites Sobranie zakonodatelstva RF 1998 No. 46, art. 5701 and Rossiyskaya Gazeta of 19 November 1998

claims.text: The Court recounts that the office of President of the RSFSR was introduced by the RSFSR Law of 24 April 1991 after the referendum of 17 March 1991 and written into the RSFSR Constitution on 24 May 1991 (five-year term, at most two consecutive terms); that on 12 June 1991 the first President of the RSFSR was elected by popular vote - 'Им стал Б.Н.Ельцин'; and that with the adoption of the RSFSR Law of 25 December 1991 on the change of the state's name and the corresponding amendments to the RSFSR Constitution 'Президент РСФСР стал именоваться Президентом Российской Федерации'.
claims.locator: Paragraph 2 of the reasoning (установил), first two sub-paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: Stated in the determination of 5 November 1998. The only reviewed source that expressly ties the retitled office to the person elected in 1991. It is retrospective and gives no single day for the change of title (it names both the 25 December 1991 law and the later constitutional amendments), so no structured date is stored. It does not merge ru_rsfsr_president and ru_president holders; Judge Morshchakova's separate opinion records disagreement on whether the two presidencies are one institution (ru_ks_134o_dissent_identity_question_19981105).

claims.text: The Court states that at the entry into force of the new Constitution '(25 декабря 1993 года)' the previously elected President of the Russian Federation held the office in his first term; from that day, as point 3 of Section Two prescribes, he began to exercise the powers it establishes; popular approval of the Constitution also settled the continued occupation of the office by the same person; he served under the new Constitution until the end of the term for which he was elected in 1991, and that first term was neither interrupted nor restarted.
claims.locator: Paragraph 2 of the reasoning, third and fourth sub-paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: Continuation service: a claim only, never a holder or a start. The passage says 'ранее избранный Президент Российской Федерации'; Yeltsin is named in the preceding and following paragraphs. The day 25 December 1993 is the Court's, not derived from the Constitution's publication rule. Judge Morshchakova's separate opinion, restating the State Duma's position, has the President exercising the new Constitution's powers 'с 1994 года'; the Court's own date stands. The dissent also records disagreement on continuation versus succession (ru_ks_134o_dissent_identity_question_19981105).

claims.text: The Court states that by a resolution of the Central Election Commission of 9 July 1996 it was officially announced that the President of the Russian Federation was considered elected to the office for a second term ('Постановлением Центральной избирательной комиссии Российской Федерации от 9 июля 1996 года было официально объявлено, что Президент Российской Федерации считается избранным на эту должность на второй срок').
claims.locator: Paragraph 3 of the reasoning, fourth sub-paragraph, first sentence
claims.uncertainty: A retrospective claim (5 November 1998) about a CEC resolution that was not itself found: no number is given, and it is not on the legal portal or in the archived CEC decree list. The CEC protocol of the same day (ru_cec_runoff_protocol_figures_19960709) gives the figures but no declaration. A result declaration is not a start. The re-election sentence of the first sub-paragraph (elections of 16 June - 3 July 1996) is not imported as a separate claim; the CEC protocols date both rounds.

claims.text: The Court states that at the official ceremony of assumption of office of the President of the Russian Federation on 9 August 1996, held under Article 82 in the presence of members of the Federation Council, State Duma deputies and Constitutional Court judges, the Chairman of the Central Election Commission announced that the President had been elected for a second term and handed him the certificate of election as President for the second term (1996-2000).
claims.locator: Paragraph 3 of the reasoning, fourth sub-paragraph
claims.uncertainty: Retrospective (5 November 1998). Ceremony context only, never a holder claim. The certificate's '1996-2000' span is the Court's description of the document, not a sourced term end. No time of day.

claims.text: The Court states that at the official ceremony of assumption of office of 9 August 1996 'избранный Президент Российской Федерации принес присягу народу': the elected President, whom the same paragraph names as the incumbent 'Б.Н.Ельцин', took the oath to the people.
claims.locator: Paragraph 3 of the reasoning, fourth sub-paragraph, last sentence
claims.uncertainty: Retrospective (5 November 1998). The oath is recorded separately from the stated assumption of office and is not used as a start; Article 92(1) is procedure and is not used to derive a date. No time of day.

claims.text: The Court states that by taking that oath at the ceremony of 9 August 1996 the elected President (Б.Н.Ельцин) 'таким образом, вступил в должность на второй срок подряд': he thereby assumed office for a second consecutive term.
claims.locator: Paragraph 3 of the reasoning, fourth sub-paragraph, last sentence
claims.uncertainty: The only reviewed source that states the day of assumption of office; it is retrospective (5 November 1998), a judicial determination rather than a contemporaneous record. It dates the holder's start. The State Duma stenogram of 10 August 1996 corroborates the ceremony day only (ru_duma_steno_inauguration_held_19960809).

claims.text: Operative point 1: proceedings are terminated for lack of uncertainty, because the President of the Russian Federation exercised his powers for a first term until the June-July 1996 elections and was elected in 1996 for a second consecutive term; the reasoning adds that transitional point 3 was exhausted in June-July 1996.
claims.locator: Operative part, point 1; paragraph 4 of the reasoning
claims.uncertainty: A judicial characterisation of terms, not a start or end date for any holder. Point 2: final, in force on proclamation.

claims.text: Judge T. G. Morshchakova's separate opinion records that the independent experts disagreed on, among other things, how continued exercise of state functions during a constitutional transition differs from succession, and whether the presidencies under the former and the current constitutions can be treated as identical institutions.
claims.locator: Separate opinion of Judge Morshchakova, point 3
claims.uncertainty: A separate opinion, not the Court's holding. It qualifies the identity of ru_rsfsr_president and ru_president and is a reason to keep their holders separate.

sources.scope_note: A primary judicial record written on 5 November 1998: every statement it makes about 1991-1996 is retrospective. Read in full (reasoning paragraphs 1-4, operative points 1-3 and Judge Morshchakova's separate opinion). Its statement of the 1996 assumption of office dates a holder start; its other statements are claims only.

sources.title: Constitution of the Russian Federation, adopted by popular vote on 12 December 1993 (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii'; the portal list cites 'Российские вести' and 'Российская газета' of 25.12.1993 among its publications

claims.text: Section Two, point 1: the Constitution enters into force on the day of its official publication following the popular vote; the day of the popular vote is deemed the day of its adoption; the 1978 Constitution (Basic Law) of the Russian Federation - Russia, as amended, ceases to have effect at the same time.
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. Neither the deemed adoption day printed in the text nor the publication rule is used as a date; the entry-into-force day is taken only from a source that states it (ru_ks_134o_continuation_new_constitution_19931225), and no structured date is stored here.

claims.text: Section Two, point 3: the President of the Russian Federation elected under the Constitution (Basic Law) of the Russian Federation - Russia exercises, from the day this Constitution enters into force, the powers it establishes until the expiry of the term for which he was elected.
claims.uncertainty: The source-stated effect on the incumbent's office, as text only: it names no person and no day, and creates continuation, not a new holder.

claims.text: Article 80(1): the President of the Russian Federation is the head of state; Article 80(4) adds that as head of state he represents the Russian Federation at home and abroad.
claims.uncertainty: Supports the head_of_state kind for ru_president under this Constitution. The RSFSR-era office was 'the highest official and head of executive power' (Law 1098-I, in ru_rsfsr_president); the classification is not backdated.

claims.text: Article 81: four-year term, not more than two consecutive terms. Article 82: on assuming office the President takes the printed oath to the people, in a solemn setting in the presence of members of the Federation Council, State Duma deputies and Constitutional Court judges. Article 92(1): the President begins to exercise his powers from the moment of taking the oath and ceases when the newly elected President takes the oath; 92(2) early cessation on resignation, persistent incapacity or removal; 92(3) the Chairman of the Government temporarily performs the duties.
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only; never used to derive a start or end. In particular, Article 92(1)'s rule that powers cease when the newly elected President takes the oath is never used to infer an end from a successor's oath. Cited from RU-PRES-02 only.

claims.text: The portal's list entry for the Constitution cites 'Российские вести' and 'Российская газета' of 25.12.1993 as publications.
claims.uncertainty: Portal metadata; neither issue was inspected (as CLAUDE-C01-05 treated the portal citation for Law 1098-I), so no structured date is set from it. Rossiyskaya Gazeta's 2004 web reproduction of the Constitution is a lead, not a source (its header lines are site template fields).

sources.scope_note: Constitution text is procedure only: nothing from it is used as a date, and none of its claims carries a structured date. Read: the heading, Articles 80-82 and 92-93, and Section Two points 1-9. The printed gazette issues of 25 December 1993 were not inspected.

sources.title: Resolution of the Federation Council No. 697-I SF of 15 November 1995 'On calling the election of the President of the Russian Federation' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii'; resolution of the Federation Council of the Federal Assembly

claims.text: Citing Article 81 and Article 102(1)(d) of the Constitution and Article 4 of the federal law on the election of the President, the Federation Council calls the election of the President of the Russian Federation for 16 June 1996. Signed V. F. Shumeiko, Chairman of the Federation Council, Moscow, 15 November 1995, No. 697-I SF.
claims.locator: Operative point; signature and date block
claims.uncertainty: A scheduling act: it fixes the voting day but does not attest that voting took place, a result or any holder. The voting day is a claim, never a term boundary.

sources.scope_note: Read in full (one operative point and the signature block). Cited in determination 134-O. It schedules the vote and attests nothing about the voting or the result.

sources.title: Protocol of the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation on the results of the election of the President of the Russian Federation, voting of 16 June 1996 (CEC election archive file 1996-1-Protokol_CIK.doc)
sources.publisher: Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation (cikrf.ru election archive)

claims.text: The protocol is headed 'ВЫБОРЫ ПРЕЗИДЕНТА РОССИЙСКОЙ ФЕДЕРАЦИИ 16 ИЮНЯ 1996 ГОДА'.
claims.uncertainty: The first-round voting day as the CEC heads the protocol; a claim, never a start.

claims.text: Summing 89 subject-commission protocols and 397 protocols of polling stations abroad, the CEC determines: 108,495,023 voters on the lists; 74,515,019 valid and 1,072,120 invalid ballots; 75,744,549 voters took part in the election; ten candidates, among them 'ЕЛЬЦИН БОРИС НИКОЛАЕВИЧ' 26,665,495 votes, 'ЗЮГАНОВ ГЕННАДИЙ АНДРЕЕВИЧ' 24,211,686 and 'ЛЕБЕДЬ АЛЕКСАНДР ИВАНОВИЧ' 10,974,736; against all 1,163,921. Chairman N. T. Ryabov heads the signature block. 'Протокол составлен "20" июня 1996 года'.
claims.uncertainty: Figures only: the protocol does not say that no candidate was elected or who advances to the run-off; that decision (CEC resolution 105/825-II of 20 June 1996) was not found in an official copy. The digital file was re-saved in 2008 and has blank signature lines. Not a start.

sources.scope_note: The CEC's election-archive copy, linked from the same archived 1996 page as the run-off protocol. The Word file's metadata gives 19-20 June 1996 and a later save on 26 September 2008, so the digital copy was edited after 1996; its signature lines are blank. Read in full after text extraction; not rendered as an image. The CEC resolution 105/825-II of 20 June 1996 on the first-round result and the run-off was not found in an official copy.

sources.title: Protocol of the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation on the results of the election of the President of the Russian Federation, repeat voting of 3 July 1996 (CEC election archive file 1996-2-Protokol_CIK.doc)
sources.publisher: Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation (cikrf.ru election archive)

claims.text: The protocol is headed 'Выборы Президента Российской Федерации. Повторное голосование 3 июля 1996 года'.
claims.uncertainty: The voting day as the CEC heads the protocol; a claim, never a start.

claims.text: The CEC, summing 89 subject-commission protocols and 397 protocols of polling stations abroad, determines: 108,600,730 voters on the lists; 73,926,240 valid and 780,405 invalid ballots; 74,815,898 voters took part in the election; 'ЕЛЬЦИН БОРИС НИКОЛАЕВИЧ' 40,208,384 votes; 'ЗЮГАНОВ ГЕННАДИЙ АНДРЕЕВИЧ' 30,113,306; against all 3,604,550. Chairman N. T. Ryabov heads the signature block. 'Протокол составлен 9 июля 1996 года'.
claims.uncertainty: Figures only: the protocol does not state who is elected, and the digital file has blank signature lines. The figures were amended by CEC resolution 112/845-II of 19 July 1996 (ru_cec_protocol_amended_dagestan_19960719) and possibly by later resolutions not reviewed. Not a start.

sources.scope_note: The CEC's election-archive copy of the run-off protocol, a Word file created 8 July and last saved 9 July 1996, with blank signature lines. Read in full after text extraction; not rendered as an image. The archive page that links it (index_response) also lists five later CEC resolutions on regional corrections, of which only 112/845-II was reviewed.

sources.title: Resolution of the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation No. 112/845-II of 19 July 1996 on the Dagestan Election Commission's resolution of 11 July 1996 amending its protocol
sources.publisher: Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation (cikrf.ru)

claims.text: After the Dagestan commission corrected its protocol on 11 July 1996, the CEC notes that the changes to that protocol and to the CEC protocol on the results of the 3 July 1996 repeat voting do not affect the result of the election nationally, and sets revised data for the CEC protocol of 9 July 1996: 108,589,050 voters on the lists; 74,800,449 took part; 'ЕЛЬЦИН Борис Николаевич' 40,203,948 (instead of 40,208,384); 'ЗЮГАНОВ Геннадий Андреевич' 30,102,288 (instead of 30,113,306); against all 3,604,462.
claims.uncertainty: Later CEC resolutions of 10 August and 8 October 1996 and of 28 March and 6 November 1997 concern further regional corrections and were not reviewed, so final national figures are not established. The signature block lists the Deputy Chairman and the Secretary.

sources.scope_note: Read in full (preamble, points 1-6 with the revised figures, signature block). Point 6 orders publication in the CEC Vestnik and dispatch to Rossiyskaya Gazeta; neither publication was inspected.

sources.title: Decree of the President of the Russian Federation No. 1138 of 5 August 1996 'On the official symbols of presidential power and their use at the assumption of office by a newly elected President of the Russian Federation'
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii'; the portal list cites Sobranie zakonodatelstva RF 1996 No. 33, art. 3976 and Rossiyskaya Gazeta of 8 August 1996

claims.text: The decree fixes the symbols of presidential power (the Standard, the Sign of the President and a specially made copy of the Constitution) and their use when a newly elected President assumes office: the President takes the oath on the special copy of the Constitution; the Chairman of the Federation Council places the Sign on him; after the oath a duplicate Standard is raised over the Kremlin residence; the symbols are handed over after the oath. In force from signature; signed by Yeltsin as President, 5 August 1996.
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only; names no ceremony day and is not used to date the oath. The decree's own signature ('Б. Ельцин', 5 August 1996) is not recorded as a separate claim.

sources.scope_note: Read in full; procedure for the ceremony only.

sources.title: State Duma: stenogram of the sitting of 10 August 1996 (Transcripts database)
sources.publisher: State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation, transcripts database (transcript.duma.gov.ru)

claims.text: At the sitting of 10 August 1996 (Great Hall, 11:00, chaired by G. N. Seleznev), deputy N. I. Ryzhkov speaks of 'Борис Николаевич Ельцин, инаугурация которого состоялась вчера', and V. V. Zhirinovsky, in a rhetorical aside, refers to the deputies having taken part 'yesterday' in the President's inauguration ('Если вчера мы участвовали в инаугурации Президента').
claims.locator: Speeches of Zhirinovsky V. V. and Ryzhkov N. I. in the debate on Chernomyrdin's nomination
claims.uncertainty: Contemporaneous, but deputies' remarks, not an official record of the ceremony; the day is the sitting's date less one ('вчера'). No oath text or time. Corroborates the ceremony day only; ceremony context, never a holder claim or an assumption of office.

sources.scope_note: The live official page (no Internet Archive capture exists), searched for 'инаугурац', 'присяг' and 'вступ... в должность'; the opening and the speeches containing the hits were read. The nomination of V. S. Chernomyrdin debated at the same sitting is outside this packet.

sources.title: Decree of the President of the Russian Federation No. 1146 of 9 August 1996 'On the resignation of the Government of the Russian Federation'
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii'; the portal list cites Sobranie zakonodatelstva RF 1996 No. 33, art. 3979 and Rossiyskaya Gazeta of 10 August 1996

claims.text: Decree No. 1146 of 9 August 1996, citing Article 116 and Article 117(5) of the Constitution, accepts the Government's statement resigning its powers and instructs it to continue acting until a new Government is formed. It is signed 'Президент Российской Федерации Б.Ельцин, Москва, Кремль, 9 августа 1996 года, № 1146'.
claims.uncertainty: A same-day signature under the title, not a presidency event: the acceptance concerns the Government's resignation (Article 116: the Government resigns before a newly elected President), not the presidency. It does not mention the oath or the inauguration and is not used to date anything; it is not a holder claim. Published text.

claims.text: Citing Article 116 and Article 117(5) of the Constitution, the decree accepts the statement of the Government of the Russian Federation resigning its powers ('Принять заявление Правительства Российской Федерации о сложении своих полномочий').
claims.uncertainty: The Government as a body; names no Chairman, and the Government's own statement is not in this source. Never an end boundary for any holder. A CLAUDE-C01-19 row on the CLAUDE-C01-14 source, cited only by ru_government and ru_government_chairman.

claims.text: The decree instructs the Government to continue acting until a new Government is formed ('продолжить действовать до сформирования нового состава Правительства').
claims.uncertainty: Continuation of the Government as a body, claim only, never a holder; names nobody. A CLAUDE-C01-19 row on the CLAUDE-C01-14 source.

sources.scope_note: Read in full. The portal's date list for 9 August 1996 (portal_card_response) holds nine acts and none on the inauguration itself. sources.title: Resolution of the Congress of People's Deputies of the RSFSR No. 1830-I of 1 November 1991 'On the organisation of executive power during the radical economic reform' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS Zakonodatelstvo Rossii; the portal card cites Ведомости Съезда народных депутатов РСФСР и Верховного Совета РСФСР от 1991 г., N 44, ст. 1455

claims.text: The Congress of People's Deputies of the RSFSR resolves that, until the RSFSR Law 'On the Council of Ministers of the RSFSR' is adopted, the President of the RSFSR decides on his own, within the budget funds allotted by the Supreme Soviet, questions of reorganising the structure of the highest bodies of executive power (point 2). The resolution takes effect on adoption and ceases on 1 December 1992 (point 5). It names nobody as head of the Government; it is signed by the Chairman of the Supreme Soviet 'Р. И. ХАСБУЛАТОВ'.
claims.locator: Point 2, first paragraph; point 5; signature block (Москва, Кремль, 1 ноября 1991 года, N 1830-I)
claims.uncertainty: An authorisation, not a designation of a head of Government; the resolution prints no ordinal for the Congress (only decree 171's preamble speaks of the Fifth Congress), and decree 171 of 6 Nov 1991 cites point 2 as its basis. A dated act of the Congress, never a holder boundary.

sources.title: Decree of the President of the RSFSR No. 171 of 6 November 1991 'On the reorganisation of the Government of the RSFSR' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS Zakonodatelstvo Rossii

claims.text: Citing Article 121-1 and Article 121-5(6) of the RSFSR Constitution and point 2 of the Congress resolution of 1 November 1991, the decree states that for the period of the economic reform the Government of the RSFSR is headed by the President of the RSFSR ('На период экономической реформы Правительство РСФСР возглавляет Президент РСФСР'). It is signed 'Президент РСФСР Б. ЕЛЬЦИН, Москва, Кремль, 6 ноября 1991 года, N 171'.
claims.uncertainty: Point 1 names the office (President of the RSFSR), not a person; the only printed name is the signature 'Б. ЕЛЬЦИН' (initial and surname). The President heads the Government ex officio; no one is given the title of Chairman. The decree states no effective day and no end other than 'the period of the economic reform'. Claim only, not a holder.

claims.text: The decree instructs the Council of Ministers of the RSFSR to carry out its duties until the new composition of the Government of the RSFSR is formed, and asks the Vice-President and the State Secretary to submit reorganisation proposals within three days.
claims.uncertainty: Continuation of the outgoing Council of Ministers, which the decree does not name or date further; claim only.

claims.text: The decree forms the Government of the RSFSR, for the period of the radical economic reform, under the direct leadership of the President of the RSFSR; its listed composition begins with the First Deputy Chairman and the Deputy Chairmen and lists no Chairman (point 1). The President heads the Government, conducts its sittings and signs its decisions (point 4); in his absence the First Deputy Chairman conducts sittings and signs resolutions on his instruction (point 2). The decree takes effect from signing (point 12) and is signed 'Президент РСФСР Б. ЕЛЬЦИН', 6 November 1991, N 172.
claims.uncertainty: As for decree 171: the provisions name the office, the only printed name is the signature. Takes effect from signing, but this is the effect of an organisational decree, not a stated assumption of a Chairman's office; the annexes (structure) are not reproduced on the portal ('Приложения не приводятся'). Claim only.

sources.title: State Duma: stenogram of the sitting of 10 August 1996 (Transcripts database, node 2898), Internet Archive capture 20240528152653
sources.publisher: State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation (transcript.duma.gov.ru); raw capture by the Internet Archive

claims.text: The presiding Chairman G. N. Seleznev tells the sitting that the President, asked by the Duma Council to present his candidate in person, proposed that the Chairman present V. S. Chernomyrdin, and reads the President's letter: under Article 111 of the Constitution 'вношу предложение о кандидатуре Черномырдина Виктора Степановича на должность Председателя Правительства Российской Федерации и прошу дать согласие на его назначение'. Earlier in the sitting deputy E. B. Mizulina says that less than a day had passed since the President's submission ('Не прошло и суток с момента внесения представления Президентом').
claims.locator: Morning session: Mizulina's remarks and the Chairman's presentation of the candidacy (before Chernomyrdin's address)
claims.uncertainty: The letter's own date is not read out; 10 August 1996 is the day it was presented to the Duma, and Mizulina's remark places the submission within the preceding day. The Chairman also mentions an order of the President that the Government resigns its powers (distributed to deputies), which is decree 1146 of 9 August in substance; no separate claim. The day of the President's submission is not given; a nomination as presented at the sitting, never used to date a holder.

claims.text: The Chairman puts the question whether to give the President consent to appoint Viktor Stepanovich Chernomyrdin Chairman of the Government, in a secret vote; the electronic result (16:21:54) reads 314 for (69.8%), 85 against (18.9%), 3 abstentions (0.7%), 402 voting, 48 not voting, 'Результат: принято'. Chernomyrdin then thanks the deputies and speaks of what will follow 'после того как будет указ о моем назначении'.
claims.locator: Afternoon: ballot formulation, 'Результаты голосования (16 час. 21 мин. 54 сек.)', Chernomyrdin's reply
claims.uncertainty: The vote precedes and is distinct from the resolution 624-II ГД and the appointment decree 1152; Chernomyrdin's own words place the appointment after the sitting.

sources.scope_note: Raw Internet Archive capture 20240528152653 of the official page, made before the cutoff. The frozen capture of the sitting recorded live by CLAUDE-C01-14 (ru_duma_steno_19960810); used here so that the two Chairman claims rest on a byte-stable response and the C01-14 extract is not edited.

claims.uncertainty: Continuation of the Government's members, not of any named Chairman; a claim only.

claims.text: Item dated 12 September 2007, 15:00, Moscow: at a meeting in the Kremlin Mikhail Fradkov asked the President for resignation ('обратился к Президенту с просьбой об отставке').

sources.title: Начало рабочей встречи с Председателем Правительства Михаилом Фрадковым (Beginning of the working meeting with Chairman of the Government Mikhail Fradkov), 12 September 2007 — kremlin.ru transcripts
sources.publisher: President of Russia official website (kremlin.ru), Presidential Executive Office

claims.text: Transcript dated 12 September 2007, 15:26, Moscow, Kremlin: speaking as М.Фрадков, he says that with parliamentary and presidential elections ahead he wants to free the post of Chairman of the Government so that the President has full freedom of decision, and asks the President for his resignation after more than three and a half years as Chairman.
claims.uncertainty: The request in his own words; not itself the end and never a boundary. The captured page carries 'Последнее обновление материала 20 марта 2015 года'.

claims.text: В.Путин replies that he fully agrees with Fradkov's assessment ('полностью согласен с Вашей оценкой') and, in his final sentence, accepts the resignation: 'Принимая Вашу отставку'.
claims.uncertainty: Acceptance in the President's words; it does not state that the powers of the Chairman ceased that day. If the integrator accepts the acceptance of a personal resignation as a stated end, this is the one claim to anchor it on; by default the 2004 Fradkov observation has no until. Putin addresses him only as 'Михаил Ефимович'; the heading names 'Председателем Правительства Михаилом Фрадковым'. The captured page carries 'Последнее обновление материала 20 марта 2015 года'.

claims.text: In the same sentence the President asks him to perform his duties until the State Duma approves the candidacy of a new Chairman of the Government ('прошу Вас вплоть до одобрения кандидатуры нового Председателя Правительства Российской Федерации Государственной Думой исполнять свои обязанности'); Фрадков thanks him and calls the decision right.
claims.locator: Putin's reply, final sentence; Fradkov's closing reply
claims.uncertainty: A request to continue performing the duties: acting service is a claim only, never a holder, with no stated end.

sources.title: «Об общественном объединении "ЯБЛОКО"» — the Yabloko association's reference page (history, leaders, congresses, registration), yabloko.ru, undated (captured 30 June 1998)
sources.publisher: Yabloko official website (yabloko.ru), read from a raw Internet Archive capture

claims.text: The association's undated reference page (captured 30 June 1998) says its Duma members entered parliament on the lists of the electoral association "Блок: Явлинский - Болдырев - Лукин" in autumn 1993 ("осенью 1993 года").
claims.uncertainty: Retrospective, season only; the bloc is named, but no bloc leader or chairman is printed. Not a record of the Central Election Commission and not a party-leader claim.

claims.text: The same page gives as former names ("Старое название") the federal electoral association "Блок: Явлинский - Болдырев - Лукин" (1993) and the State Duma faction "Яблоко" (1994).
claims.uncertainty: A retrospective name lineage with years only. It does not establish that the bloc, the Duma faction and the association are one legal identity, and a faction is never a party office.

claims.text: The same page says the founding congress ("Учредительный съезд") of the all-Russian public political association "Яблоко" was held on 5-6 January 1995 near Moscow ("5-6 января 1995 г. в Подмосковье").
claims.uncertainty: Retrospective (page of about 1998); a two-day span with no structured date. No contemporaneous 1995 congress record was found.

claims.text: The same page says the founding congress formed the governing bodies, among them the chairman of the movement ("председатель движения (им стал Г.Явлинский)") and two vice-chairmen (Ю.Болдырев and В.Лукин).
claims.uncertainty: Retrospective; the day of the election within 5-6 January 1995 is not printed. An election is never a holder date or start.

claims.text: The same page lists under "Руководители": "Председатель объединения - Явлинский Григорий Алексеевич (с января 1995 г.)".
claims.uncertainty: An undated retrospective list with a month-only start; a claim, never a boundary or a holder date.

claims.text: The same page states the association's registration: "10 февраля 1995 г., регистрационный номер 2554".
claims.uncertainty: The association's own statement of its registration, not the Ministry of Justice register (minjust.gov.ru answered 403). An organization event, never a holder boundary.

sources.scope_note: Undated reference page of the association, read in full from the capture; its statements about 1993-1995 are retrospective. Footer "Copiright (c) 1998 Yabloko".

institutions.name: Presidency of the RSFSR (Президент РСФСР)

jurisdiction.note: An office of the RSFSR, which Law 2094-I of 25 December 1991 renamed the Russian Federation (Russia). It is not the USSR Presidency (ussr.json su_presidency); no transfer from any USSR institution is recorded or inferred.

source_identifier.note: Law of the RSFSR of 24 April 1991 creating the office; a research locator, not a registry identifier.

institutions.identity_note: The office created by RSFSR Law 1098-I and written into the RSFSR Constitution as Chapter 13-1. It is filed in the Russia packet because Law 2094-I renamed the RSFSR itself; that is a sourced renaming of the same republic, not a succession from the USSR. The Russian-language title is the statutory one.

lifecycle.note: Law 1098-I was adopted on 24 April 1991. Resolution 1099-I of the same day put it into force from the moment of publication, and that day is not verified (the portal card cites Rossiyskaya Gazeta of 27 April 1991, which was not inspected). The Congress approved the law on 22 May 1991 (1324-I) and wrote Chapter 13-1 into the RSFSR Constitution on 24 May 1991 (1326-I). Each is a separate dated claim. None is used as the office's start: 24 April is an adoption day, not entry into force. No end is recorded.

roles.title: President of the RSFSR (Президент РСФСР)

holder_claims.name: Борис Николаевич Ельцин
holder_claims.note: Boris Nikolaevich Yeltsin, named as in resolution 1595-I. He takes office from the oath at the solemn session of 10 July 1991 (Law 1494-I, Article 3; stenogram, printed page 6); resolution 1595-I of the same day cites his assumption of office.
holder_claims.uncertainty: Day precision: the session opened at 10:00 and the minute of the oath is not printed. No end date or term is recorded; the five-year rule is not used to infer one, and later events are outside this packet. The 12 June vote and the 19 June result are separate claims, not the start.

roles.scope_note: The statute calls the President the highest official and head of executive power in the RSFSR; no head-of-state or head-of-government classification is inferred. The election, the result and the oath are separate dated claims.

roles.scope_note: Elected jointly with the President; takes office from the President's oath under Law 1494-I.

roles.title: Президент Российской Федерации — President of the Russian Federation

holder_claims.name: Борис Николаевич Ельцин
holder_claims.note: Boris Nikolaevich Yeltsin, named as in the C01-05 holder (resolution 1595-I) and the State Duma stenogram of 10 August 1996; determination 134-O prints 'Б.Н.Ельцин' and decree 1761 'Б.Ельцин'. From 9 August 1996: Constitutional Court determination 134-O states that at the ceremony that day he took the oath to the people 'и, таким образом, вступил в должность' for a second consecutive term. Until 31 December 1999: decree 1761, signed by him as President, states that he ceases to exercise the powers of the President from 12:00 on 31 December 1999.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start rests on a retrospective judicial statement of 5 November 1998; neither a contemporaneous official record of the oath nor the CEC resolution of 9 July 1996 that declared the result was found. If the reviewer does not accept a later court statement as a start, the fallback is attested_on 1996-08-09 with from null. The calling of the election, both votes, both protocols, the declaration and the ceremony are separate claims, not the start. The end is stated by the decree to the hour (12:00 Moscow time); the resignation address, decree 1762's reference and Federation Council resolution 4-SF are separate claims. Never merged with the C01-05 ru_rsfsr_president holder, and no 1991-1996 observation on this role is recorded.

holder_claims.name: Владимир Владимирович Путин
holder_claims.note: Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin, named as in the declaration. From 7 May 2000: in the Kremlin transcript of the ceremony, Constitutional Court Chairman M. Baglai declares, immediately after the oath, that 'Владимир Владимирович Путин' has assumed the office of President of the Russian Federation; the transcript is dated 7 May 2000, and the site's news item of 13:00 that day reports that the ceremony of assumption took place.
holder_claims.uncertainty: Day precision: the news item has him on the podium at noon, and the minute of the oath is not printed. His acting service from 12:00 on 31 December 1999 is claims only and is not joined to this observation; no source states when it ended. The 26 March vote, the 5 April declaration and the ceremony are separate claims. No end is set; his 2004 assumption is a separate observation and is not used as an end.

holder_claims.name: Владимир Владимирович Путин
holder_claims.note: From 7 May 2004: in the Kremlin broadcast transcript, Constitutional Court Chairman V. D. Zorkin declares after the oath that 'Владимир Владимирович Путин' has assumed the office of President of the Russian Federation. The page carries only a header date; the site's news item stamped 7 May 2004, 13:30 reports that the ceremony of assumption took place that day.
holder_claims.uncertainty: Day precision; no clock time is printed. The 14 March vote, the 23 March declaration and its three later corrections, and the ceremony are separate claims. No end is set: his statement of 7 May 2008 ('Сейчас, слагая с себя полномочия главы государства'), spoken before Medvedev's oath, does not state that the office had ended, and Medvedev's assumption is not used as an end.

holder_claims.name: Дмитрий Анатольевич Медведев
holder_claims.note: Dmitry Anatolyevich Medvedev, named as in Zorkin's declaration. From 7 May 2008: Zorkin declares after the oath that 'Дмитрий Анатольевич Медведев вступил в должность Президента России' (broadcast transcript), and the Kremlin item of 12:20 that day is headed 'Дмитрий Медведев вступил в должность Президента России'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: Day precision. The 2 March vote, the 7 March declaration, its publication and the oath are separate claims. No end is set: his remarks at the 2012 ceremony ('Завершая работу на посту главы государства'; 'сегодня Президентом станет Владимир Владимирович Путин') were spoken before Putin's oath and do not state that his office had ended, and Putin's 2012 assumption is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Владимир Владимирович Путин
holder_claims.note: From 7 May 2012: Zorkin declares after the oath that 'Владимир Владимирович Путин вступил в должность Президента России' (Kremlin item of 12:30 with the ceremony transcript).
holder_claims.uncertainty: Day precision. The 4 March vote, the 7 March declaration, its publication and the oath are separate claims. No end is set; his 2018 assumption is a separate observation and is not used as an end.

holder_claims.name: Владимир Владимирович Путин
holder_claims.note: From 7 May 2018: the Kremlin item headed 'Владимир Путин вступил в должность Президента России' states that Zorkin announced his assumption of office as President of the Russian Federation.
holder_claims.uncertainty: Day precision. The 18 March vote, the 23 March declaration, its publication and the oath are separate claims. No end is set; his 2024 assumption is a separate observation and is not used as an end.

holder_claims.name: Владимир Владимирович Путин
holder_claims.note: From 7 May 2024: the Kremlin item headed 'Владимир Путин вступил в должность Президента России' states that Zorkin announced his assumption of office as President of the Russian Federation. The latest in-office attestation reviewed before the cutoff is decree No. 636 of 4 September 2026, signed 'Президент Российской Федерации В.Путин' and officially published that day.
holder_claims.uncertainty: Day precision. The 15-17 March voting, the 21 March declaration and the oath are separate claims. In office at the cutoff by attestation only: the decree of 4 September 2026 is not a boundary, and no end is set or inferred.

roles.scope_note: Head of state under Article 80(1) of the 1993 Constitution (ru_const1993_art80_head_of_state). The title 'Президент Российской Федерации' replaced 'Президент РСФСР' through the state's renaming (Law 2094-I, recorded at institution level by CLAUDE-C01-05) and Law 2708-I of 21 April 1992; Constitutional Court determination 134-O (5 November 1998) states that the President of the RSFSR 'стал именоваться' President of the Russian Federation and names Yeltsin as the person elected in 1991. That retrospective tie is a claim: no holder is carried over or merged from ru_rsfsr_president, whose C01-05 holders are unchanged, and no ru_president holder is recorded for 1991-1996 (the 1992-1993 stylings under the new title and the 25 December 1993 continuation are claims only). Election calling, voting, CEC protocols, declarations, corrections and publications, inauguration ceremonies, outgoing-holder statements, retrospective narration and acting service are claims, never holders or boundaries; the Chairman of the Government's acting service from 31 December 1999 is claims only. Constitution and statute texts are procedure only, never a date. A holder has from only where a source states the day office was assumed and until only where a source states the day it ended.

unresolved: SURU-TR91-01: the publication that brought Law 1098-I into force (probably Rossiyskaya Gazeta of 27 April 1991, not inspected) and the RSFSR protocol of the 17 March 1991 referendum question on the presidency are unverified; lifecycle.from stays null.

SURU-TR91-02: the TASS or press publication of the CEC communication, the 'official announcement' from which Law 1494-I counts one month, is not dated. The GARF leaf numbering of the CEC record (captions L. 6, 6 ob. and 7; handwritten folios 5, 6 and 7) is unconfirmed.

SURU-TR91-03: both holders start on 10 July 1991 with no end. The August 1991 events, the 1993 status of the office and any later terms are outside this packet; no end is inferred from the five-year rule.

Law 2094-I renamed the RSFSR itself and is not a succession from the USSR. Its signed original reads 'President of the RSFSR', while the published text prints 'President of the Russian Federation'. The USSR Presidency, Supreme Soviet and Congress are not mapped to this or any Russia institution.

RU-PRES-01 (CLAUDE-C01-14): determination 134-O (1998) ties the retitled office to Yeltsin, and records of 1992-1993 style him President of the Russian Federation, but no ru_president holder is recorded for 1991-1996 and no holder is merged across ru_rsfsr_president and ru_president. Whether to add a dated 1992-1993 observation, or to treat the two roles as one retitled office, is an integrator decision. The publication day that brought Law 2708-I into force, its signed original and whether the heading of Chapter 13-1 was retitled are unverified.

RU-PRES-02: the 1993 Constitution's entry into force on 25 December 1993 and the incumbent's continuation rest on 134-O's statement (claims only); Rossiyskaya Gazeta No. 237 of 25 December 1993 as printed was not inspected.

RU-PRES-03: the CEC resolution of 9 July 1996 that declared the run-off result (known only from 134-O), CEC resolution 105/825-II of 20 June 1996 on the first round, and a contemporaneous official record of the 9 August 1996 oath were not found; Yeltsin's 1996 start rests on 134-O. Final 1996 figures after the CEC corrections of August 1996 - November 1997 are not established.
RU-PRES-04: no reviewed source states when the acting service that began at 12:00 on 31 December 1999 ended; it is not inferred from the 7 May 2000 assumption of office.

RU-PRES-05: the result resolution of 5 April 2000 is numbered 98/1110-3 in Rossiyskaya Gazeta's official section and 97/1110-3 in the CEC's April 2000 list; the difference and the gazette issue date are unresolved.

RU-PRES-05 to 10: the minute of each oath and stated assumption of office is not printed (day precision only). No source states an end for the 2000, 2004, 2012, 2018 or 2024 Putin observations or for Medvedev's 2008 observation; outgoing statements made before the successor's oath are claims, not ends, and no end is inferred from a successor's start. The latest in-office attestation reviewed is decree No. 636 of 4 September 2026.

RU-PRES-07 to 10: gazette pages cited only on portal cards (Sobranie zakonodatelstva, Parlamentskaya Gazeta and Rossiyskaya Gazeta issues for the Federation Council resolutions and decrees) were not inspected; the CEC's own 2024 result page is unavailable.

institutions.name: Правительство Российской Федерации — Government of the Russian Federation

jurisdiction.note: The federal Government of the RSFSR and of the Russian Federation as printed in the reviewed acts: 'Правительство РСФСР' (November 1991), 'Правительство Российской Федерации' (June-July 1992 and 1996-2026) and 'Совет Министров - Правительство Российской Федерации' (December 1992). It is not the USSR Cabinet of Ministers or Council of Ministers (ussr.json); no transfer from any USSR institution is recorded or inferred.

source_identifier.note: The name printed in the decrees, resolutions and orders reviewed; a research locator, not a registry identifier.

institutions.identity_note: Filed as one executive institution for the Chairman of the Government role reviewed in CLAUDE-C01-19. The printed titles vary across 1991-2026 (see jurisdiction); no creation, retitling or dissolution date is established here, and the Congress of People's Deputies and the State Duma appear only as the authors of dated claims, not as institutions.

lifecycle.note: No creation, retitling or end of the Government is established by this packet. Decrees 171 and 172 of 6 November 1991 reorganise the Government of the RSFSR under the President (claims only); the Government's dismissals, resignations and the laying down of its powers before each newly elected President are dated claims about the body, not lifecycle boundaries. Constitution and statute texts are procedure only and are not used for dates.

holder_claims.name: Виктор Степанович Черномырдин

holder_claims.uncertainty: No effect clause, so from is null. The President's letter as presented, the Duma vote and resolution 624-II ГД of the same day are separate claims. Decree 281 of 23 March 1998 announces the Government's resignation without naming him, so there is no until; his acting service from 23 August 1998 (decree 983) is claims only and is not joined to this observation.

holder_claims.note: Sergei Vladilenovich Kiriyenko, named as in decree 436 ('Кириенко Сергея Владиленовича', accusative). Attested on 24 April 1998: decree 436 appoints him Chairman of the Government.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No effect clause, so from is null. The three presentations of his candidacy, the two failed consent votes, the secret ballot of 24 April and resolution 2421-II ГД are separate claims; his acting service from 23 March 1998 (decree 288) is claims only. roles.scope_note: The Chairman of the Government. The President's nomination, its presentation at a Duma sitting, the Congress's or the State Duma's consent, approval or refusal and the vote, the appointment decree, the Government's resignation, dismissal or laying down of its powers, continued duties, acting service and in-office attestations are separate dated claims. A holder has from only where the appointment decree states that it takes effect on signing (1999-2024); the 1992-1998 decrees and decree 611 of 1999 have no effect clause, so those holders carry attested_on only. No holder has an until: no reviewed source states the day a Chairman's office ended, and no end is taken from a successor's appointment, a dismissal or resignation of the Government, the laying down of its powers or an acting designation. Acting and continuing service are claims only, never holders or boundaries; the 1991-1992 arrangement under which the President headed the Government is claims only. Constitution and statute texts are procedure only, never a date. The presidency roles of ru_rsfsr_presidency are unchanged and share no holder with this role.

unresolved: RU-GOV-01: when the 1991 arrangement under which the President headed the Government ended is not stated (the portal marks decrees 171 and 172 'Утратил силу' without the repealing act); decree 1569 says only that the Chairman's post was vacant until 14 December 1992. Yeltsin's heading of the Government and Gaidar's acting service (15 June - 15 December 1992) are claims only.

RU-GOV-02: the President's 1992 and 1996 nomination letters and the candidate and result of the Congress's secret ballot of 9 December 1992 (resolution 4063-I names nobody) are not established, and no Congress stenogram was found. The 1993 change of the title 'Председатель Совета Министров - Правительства Российской Федерации' is not reviewed.

RU-GOV-03: the President's letters of 1998 and their dates are not established (the three submissions are attested as presented at the sittings of 10, 17 and 24 April 1998); the order of signing of decrees 281, 287 and 288 of 23 March 1998 is not stated; no source names Chernomyrdin at the 23 March dismissal or states the day his office ended.
RU-GOV-04: no source states the day Kiriyenko's office ended (decree 983 names no Chairman) or when Chernomyrdin's acting service from 23 August 1998 ended.

RU-GOV-03 and 04: the stenograms of 24 April and 31 August 1998 are live pages whose footer prints the current year, so their recorded identities are expected to stop reproducing on 1 January 2027; no usable Internet Archive capture made before the cutoff exists. The CLAUDE-C01-14 stenogram of 10 August 1996 has the same footer; this packet cites the frozen capture of that sitting instead.

RU-GOV-05: the dates of the President's nominations of Stepashin and Putin (1999) are not established (the Duma stenograms of 19 May and 16 August 1999 were behind the transcripts server's bot protection); no source names Stepashin at the 9 August 1999 dismissal or states the day his office or Primakov's ended.

RU-GOV-06: no source states when Putin's 1999 appointment or Kasyanov's 2000 appointment ended; kremlin.ru's styling of Kasyanov as former Chairman on 24 February 2004 (a page last updated in 2015) is a claim, not an end. The Duma stenogram of 17 May 2000 (vote figures) was not read.

RU-GOV-07: the formal submission letter of March 2004 is not established (kremlin.ru records only the 1 March proposal); no source states that Fradkov's office ended on 7 May 2004 or on 12 September 2007. An integrator ruling is requested on whether the President's acceptance of his resignation on 12 September 2007 is a stated end (default: no until). The kremlin.ru items of 2000-2012 carry 2014-2015 last-update stamps; no contemporaneous capture was found.

RU-GOV-08 to 10: no source states the day the office of Zubkov (2007), Putin (2008), Medvedev (2012, 2018) or Mishustin (2020) ended; the Government's orders laying down its powers (2008, 2012, 2018, 2024) and decree 14 of 15 January 2020 concern the Government as a body. The acting signatory of 7 May 2012 is attested (order 760-r, 'В.Зубков') but no act assigning the duties was found, and no act assigning Mishustin acting duties after 7 May 2024 was found. The State Duma's own vote records for 2007, 2008, 2012, 2018 and 2020 were not read (the 2008 and 2012 figures are kremlin.ru reports).

The latest in-office attestation reviewed is Government resolution 1125 of 3 September 2026, signed by М.Мишустин as Chairman; it is not a boundary. This packet establishes no current roster, succession eligibility or artwork claim.

Five parliamentary leader observations are not party-leader histories. Complete terms, national-executive offices, biographical identities and any portrait permission remain unresolved.
The five faction memberships are reported as 324, 57, 28, 23 and 15. They are preserved without forcing a chamber-capacity total or treating them as party election results.
All game-party mappings and faction constituent links remain empty. Shared names do not create an automatic legal identity match.
Russia and USSR organizations, predecessor states, renames, mergers, dissolutions and regional party histories require separate sourced reconciliation; no continuity is assumed.
This packet does not establish a September 2026 current roster, complete country census, succession eligibility or artwork completion. No post-cutoff facts or fictional successors are populated.

CLAUDE-C01-05 adds one institution, ru_rsfsr_presidency, from RSFSR acts of 1991. It is filed here because Law 2094-I renamed the RSFSR the Russian Federation; it is not mapped from, and does not continue, the USSR Presidency in ussr.json.

The RSFSR Supreme Soviet, its Chairman and the RSFSR Congress of People's Deputies are not institutions in this packet. Yeltsin's 1991 signatures as Supreme Soviet Chairman and his release from that post on 10 July 1991 are recorded as claims only.

CLAUDE-C01-14 adds the role ru_president (President of the Russian Federation, head_of_state) to ru_rsfsr_presidency, with seven holder observations from 1996 to 2024 drawn from official records of 1992-2026. It does not change the C01-05 holders, does not merge holders across the RSFSR and Russian Federation titles, records acting service (1999-2000) as claims only and establishes no current roster, succession eligibility or artwork claim.

CLAUDE-C01-19 adds one institution, ru_government (Government of the Russian Federation), with one role, ru_government_chairman (head_of_government), and fifteen holder observations from 1992 to 2024 drawn from official records of 1991-2026. It does not change the presidency holders, records acting service and the Government's continued duties as claims only, gives no holder an end (no reviewed source states the day a Chairman's office ended) and establishes no current roster, succession eligibility or artwork claim.

It records 24 holder observations of ten people from party records of 1994-2026 (retrospective party claims reach back to 1990), keeps congresses, elections, registrations, reorganisations, the 2022 death and interim, the 2008 accession and the 2001 dissolution as claims only, gives no holder a from or an until, and establishes no organization identity, lifecycle, game mapping, current roster, succession eligibility or artwork claim.
